title: Lagrangian Schrödinger Model and Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner
body_html:
Lagrangian Schrödinger Model and Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner

This node gives an explicit realization of the finite Heisenberg–Weil representation on the functions attached to a Lagrangian, together with the canonical intertwiner between the realizations attached to two Lagrangians. It is the concrete counterpart of the abstract class $W_\xi^{E,j}$ of Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field: that node fixes the representation only up to isomorphism, while a realization requires a polarization. The family of these realizations, with the intertwiners below, is the "unified model" in which one writes formulas; the price of the polarization is recorded in the composition law.

Setup

Let $k$ be a finite field of odd order, $(E,j)$ a nondegenerate symplectic $k$-space of dimension $2m$, $i=j/2$, and $H(E,j)=E\times k$ the Heisenberg group of Symplectic Heisenberg Group over a Finite Field with $(w,z)(w',z')=(w+w',z+z'+i(w,w'))$. Fix a nontrivial central character $\xi\colon k\to R^{\times}$, where $R$ is a coefficient field with $\operatorname{char}R\neq p$ containing the values of $\xi$ (an additive character of $k$). By Finite Heisenberg Stone-von Neumann Property the irreducible representation $\eta_\xi$ of central character $\xi$ is unique up to isomorphism, of dimension $|E|^{1/2}=q^{m}$.

A Lagrangian $L\subseteq E$ is a maximal isotropic subspace: $j(L,L)=0$ and $\dim_k L=m$, so $|L|=|E/L|=q^m$.

The Schrödinger model $\mathcal S_L$

The subgroup $H(L)=L\times k$ is abelian (since $L$ is isotropic), and $\tilde\xi_L(a,z):=\xi(z)$ is a character of it. Define

$$ \mathcal S_L:=\operatorname{ind}_{H(L)}^{H(E,j)}\tilde\xi_L, $$

realized concretely as the functions on $E$ transforming under $L$ by the cocycle:

$$ \mathcal S_L=\big\{\varphi\colon E\to R \ \big|\ \varphi(v+a)=\xi\!\big(i(v,a)\big)\,\varphi(v)\ \ \forall a\in L\big\}, \qquad \dim_R\mathcal S_L=|E/L|=q^{m}. $$

The Heisenberg group acts by

$$ \big(\eta_\xi(u,s)\varphi\big)(v)=\xi\!\big(s+i(u,v)\big)\,\varphi(v-u),\qquad (u,s)\in H(E,j). $$

(Both formulas are obtained from the induced-representation model $f(h(a,z))=\xi(z)^{-1}f(h)$, $\varphi(v)=f(v,0)$: $(v,0)(a,0)=(v+a,i(v,a))$ gives the covariance, and $(u,s)^{-1}(v,0)=(v-u,-s-i(u,v))$ gives the action.) By Stone–von Neumann $\mathcal S_L$ is a model of $\eta_\xi$, and the Weil representation $W_\xi^{E,j}$ of $S(E,j)$ acts on the same space extending $\eta_\xi$.

The change-of-Lagrangian intertwiner

For two Lagrangians \(L,L'\) define \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\colon\mathcal S_{L'}\to\mathcal S_L\) by

$$ \big(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi\big)(v)=\sum_{a\in L/(L\cap L')}\xi\!\big(i(a,v)\big)\,\varphi(v+a). $$

The verification that this formula is well-defined and \(H(E,j)\)-equivariant is isolated in Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner for Finite Schrödinger Models. The self-contained Hom-line calculation One-Dimensional Hom Line for Finite Schrödinger Models then shows

$$ \operatorname{Hom}_{H(E,j)}(\mathcal S_{L'},\mathcal S_L) =R\cdot\mathcal F_{L,L'}. $$

Thus the displayed sum fixes a normalization of the unique intertwiner line. When \(L\cap L'=0\) (transverse), \(E=L\oplus L'\) and the sum is the finite Fourier transform with kernel \(\xi\circ i\).

Composition: the Weil index

For three Lagrangians, \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\circ\mathcal F_{L',L''}\) and \(\mathcal F_{L,L''}\) are both \(H(E,j)\)-intertwiners \(\mathcal S_{L''}\to\mathcal S_L\), hence proportional:

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}\circ\mathcal F_{L',L''}=\gamma(L,L',L'')\cdot\mathcal F_{L,L''},\qquad \gamma(L,L',L'')\in R^{\times}. $$

The scalar $\gamma$ is the finite Weil index attached to this raw normalization. It measures the failure of the raw intertwiners $\mathcal F_{L,L'}$ to compose strictly. The detailed calculation is split out in Orthogonality and Trivialization of the Change-of-Lagrangian Cocycle: after fixing a base Lagrangian $L_0$, the cocycle is a coboundary and the rescaled operators form a compatible system. Thus the raw Fourier normalization has a cocycle, but the finite-field Lagrangian cocycle is not an unavoidable obstruction once a base trivialization is chosen.

Why this is the page to start from

Writing any transition map between generalized lattice models requires realizing $\mathbf S(\mathsf b)$ for the finite symplectic quotients $\mathsf b$ on both sides at once. The models $\mathcal S_L$ together with the intertwiners $\mathcal F_{L,L'}$ are that common framework: a Lagrangian $L$ is the finite shadow of a self-dual lattice $A$, and $\mathcal F_{L,L'}$ is the finite shadow of a change of $A$. The next node isolates the one property that the $A$-independence of the lattice-model transition rests on: $\gamma$ (equivalently $\mathcal F$) is invariant under symplectic reduction by an isotropic subspace contained in both Lagrangians.
